Monk
Core Monk Traits
Primary Ability Dexterity and Wisdom
Hit Point Die D8 per Monk level
Saving Throw
Proficiencies

weapons that have the Light
property

Tools or Musical Instrument (see
“Equipment”)
Armor Training None
Starting Equipment Choose A or B: (A) Spear, 5
Daggers, Artisan’s Tools or
Musical Instrument chosen
for the tool proficiency above,
Explorer’s Pack, and 11 GP; or

Becoming a Monk …
As a Level 1 Character
• Gain all the traits in the Core Monk Traits table.
• Gain the Monk’s level 1 features, which are listed
in the Monk Features table.
As a Multiclass Character
• Gain the Hit Point Die trait from the Core Monk
Traits table.
• Gain the Monk’s level 1 features, which are listed
in the Monk Features table.
Monk Class Features
As a Monk, you gain the following class features
when you reach the specified Monk levels. These
features are listed in the Monk Features table.

features.name: Martial Arts

rules.text:
Level 1: Martial Arts
Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of
combat styles that use your Unarmed Strike and
Monk weapons, which are the following:
• Simple Melee weapons
• Martial Melee weapons that have the Light
property
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only Monk weapons and you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield.
Bonus Unarmed Strike.
You can make an Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action.
Martial Arts Die.
You can roll 1d6 in place of the
normal damage of your Unarmed Strike or Monk
weapons. This die changes as you gain Monk levels,
as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk
Features table.
Dexterous Attacks.
You can use your Dexterity
modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the
attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes
and Monk weapons. In addition, when you use the
Grapple or Shove option of your Unarmed Strike,
you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your
Strength modifier to determine the save DC.

features.name: Monk’s Focus

rules.text:
Level 2: Monk’s Focus
Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself.
This energy is represented by Focus Points. Your
Monk level determines the number of points you
have, as shown in the Focus Points column of the
Monk Features table.
You can expend these points to enhance or fuel
certain Monk features. You start knowing three
such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and
Step of the Wind, each of which is detailed below.
When you expend a Focus Point, it is unavailable
until you finish a Short or Long Rest, at the end of
which you regain all your expended points.
Some features that use Focus Points require your
target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals 8
plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus.

You can expend 1 Focus Point to
make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action.

features.name: Uncanny Metabolism

rules.text:
Level 2: Uncanny Metabolism
When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your
Martial Arts die, and regain a number of Hit Points
equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again
until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Deflect Attacks

rules.text:
Level 3: Deflect Attacks
When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage,
you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack’s total
damage against you. The reduction equals 1d10 plus
your Dexterity modifier and Monk level.
If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1
Focus Point to redirect some of the attack’s force.
If you do so, choose a creature you can see within 5
feet of yourself if the attack was a melee attack or a
creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that
isn’t behind Total Cover if the attack was a ranged
attack. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity
saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of
your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier.
The damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. The Warrior of the Open Hand subclass is detailed after this

the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Monk level or lower.

features.name: Stunning Strike

rules.text:
Level 5: Stunning Strike
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk
weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 1
Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target
must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed
save, the target has the Stunned condition until the
start of your next turn. On a successful save, the
target’s Speed is halved until the start of your next
turn, and the next attack roll made against the target before then has Advantage.

retained_runtime_seed.name: Monk
retained_runtime_seed.description: SRD 5.2.1 Monk with partial levels 1-20 mechanics. Unsupported terrain, falling, Open Hand Technique, Quivering Palm and Epic Boon choices remain unavailable.

1.name: Martial Arts
1.description: While unarmored, without a shield, and using only Monk weapons, use Dexterity for attacks and damage and a d6 Martial Arts die (d8 at level 5, d10 at level 11, d12 at level 17). Monk weapons are Simple Melee weapons and Light Martial Melee weapons. You can make an Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action.

1.name: Unarmored Defense
1.description: While you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

1.name: Bonus Unarmed Strike
1.description: You can make an Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action.

1.name: Dexterous Attacks
1.description: You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons.

1.name: Martial Arts Die
1.description: You can roll your Martial Arts die in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strike or Monk weapons (1d6 at levels 1-4, 1d8 at 5-10, 1d10 at 11-16, 1d12 at 17-20).

2.name: Flurry of Blows
2.description: Spend 1 Focus to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action (three strikes at level 10+ with Heightened Focus). No preceding Attack action is required.

2.name: Patient Defense
2.description: Disengage as a Bonus Action for free, or spend 1 Focus to Disengage and Dodge together. At level 10+, also grants Temporary Hit Points equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

2.name: Step of the Wind
2.description: Dash as a Bonus Action for free, or spend 1 Focus to Dash and Disengage together.

2.name: Unarmored Movement
2.description: While you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield, your speed increases by 10 ft (+2 tiles). This bonus increases to +15 ft at level 6, +20 ft at level 10, +25 ft at level 14, and +30 ft at level 18.

2.name: Monk's Focus
2.description: You have a pool of Focus Points equal to your Monk level. Restored on Short or Long Rest.

2.name: Uncanny Metabolism
2.description: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Focus Points and regain HP equal to your Monk level plus a roll of your Martial Arts die. Once per Long Rest.

3.name: Deflect Attacks
3.description: When an attack hits you, take a Reaction to reduce damage by 1d10 + Dexterity modifier + Monk level. If reduced to 0, expend 1 Focus to redirect the attack (target makes Dex save vs Monk DC or takes 2 Martial Arts dice + Dex mod damage). At level 13 Deflect Energy extends this to any damage type.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1, up to the maximum of 20.

4.name: Slow Fall
4.description: Use your Reaction when you fall to reduce any falling damage by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

5.name: Stunning Strike
5.description: Once per turn after a Monk weapon or Unarmed Strike hits, spend 1 Focus. A failed Constitution save Stuns until your next turn begins. A successful save halves Speed and grants Advantage to the next attack against the target before then.
